take_homes: The agent's picks are guesses that fill gaps, and its self-review goes easy on itself. I check claims against what I know, or get a cold second reader.
Capture what worked in a rules file, then retro it and sharpen it every round. That file is the thing I can reuse.
Before Module 2 I need a three-line handoff: my challenge, a source the agent can read, and how I plan before it writes files.

monday.move: Run the pilot-cohort brief again with fresh data. Have the agent write a rules file from it, then get a cold read on the draft, and send it to the pricing working group.

monday.when: Monday morning, before the pricing working group
monday.stop_condition: The cold reader flags a claim I can't source, or the rules file doesn't match how I actually did the brief
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files, so the rules file will live on my machine.

misconception.why: The takeaway was the file the agent reads next time, not the prompt I typed. I still think wording matters, but the context and rules do more.

one_line: The rules-file and cold-read parts are worth the hour, but the same 'A note on context' paragraph repeats about ten times and the first half is stuff I already knew from chat.
